To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Conventional pig systems had lower global environmental impact (global warming, land use) per kg of pig meat, whereas differentiated systems (traditional and organic) had lower local impact (eutrophication) per hectare of land used.”

the impacts of non-conventional systems per kg of live weight were 4 to 54% higher for global warming potential, 5% higher for acidification, 0 to 23% higher for eutrophication potential, 0 to +11% higher for energy use and 16 to 156% higher for land occupation.

conventional pig production systems have lower global impacts, expressed per kg LW of pig produced, whereas differentiated pig production systems have a lower impact on the local environment, expressed per ha of used land.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of environmental impacts of different pig farming systems.
the environmental impact of the different systems.
the environmental impact of pig production in Europe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in terms of environmental impact, the choice of farming system depends on the impact category, and the way in which impacts are expressed (per kg of product or per ha of land).
the environmental performance of pig farming systems depends on the environmental impact category and the way the impacts are calculated and expressed.
differentiated pig production systems, with a focus on animal welfare, have lower impacts on local environment, but higher on global environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most environmentally friendly pig farming systems are those with the highest feed conversion efficiency and those that use outdoor areas most efficiently.

, for a given level of production, the environmental impacts per unit of production of a conventional farm can be lower than for an alternative farm, depending on the environmental impact category and the way in which it is expressed.
, compared with conventional systems, the environmental impact of non-conventional systems is generally higher when calculated per kg LW and generally lower when calculated per ha of land.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of system should be based on a comprehensive evaluation of the environmental impacts, including both global and local aspects.
, in the case of pig production systems, it is not possible to identify a system that is best in terms of all environmental impact categories.
it is possible to reduce environmental impacts by using non-conventional systems, but the impact reductions are not always straightforward to achieve and depend on the impact category and the system.
